e64944aa15d3e23148a1086c9719b15bc47f3eb7: Tavascan is a modest, confidential resort — 7 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and lift queues that simply don't exist. Tavascan's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Tavascan's altitude (1,750 m at the base, 2,250 m at the top) helps it keep reasonable snow cover through midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. With a day lift pass at just €22, Tavascan is one of the most affordable destinations in Spain. For families on a careful budget, or skiers who want to fit in plenty of outings without breaking the bank, it's an honest and often overlooked address. In short: Tavascan doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that's well worth (re)discovering.

e65362b903791ec9acf0e526e9f488d97d583930: Hochkössen is a small, low-key resort, with 21.7 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Hochkössen's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Hochkössen's moderate altitude, from 613 m at the village to 1688 m at the summit, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you travel is strongly advised. At €50, the day lift pass places Hochkössen among the intermediate resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies the price for most skiers. In short, Hochkössen does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
e6580ac552c3f9f2def46ef91cdff662c472019f: La Molina and Masella share the Tosa d'Alp in Catalan Cerdagne and together form Alp 2500, 145 km of runs between 1600 and 2537 m. La Molina is the doyenne of Spanish resorts — its first commercial drag lift dates from 1943 — and it even has its own station on the Puigcerdà line, two hours from Barcelona. Masella, on the north-facing slope, spreads most of its runs among the mountain pines and offers the largest night-skiing area in the Pyrenees. The summit of the Tosa links the two resorts, skis on feet.
